title: A Wolf for the Oath
premise: Freya Delacroix carves bones that whisper the names of the dead, and as ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Trades she has always kept her gift hidden behind ink and ivory. When the crown declares the Hunt — a sanctioned purge of everyone with the gift — the guild's own ledgers become the list of the condemned, and Freya flees with a disgraced oath-keeper, Wren, whose sworn duty is to deliver her to the pyre. Their only escape lies through a door back into Vhalen, the drowned country erased from the map, where the dead are not dead but waiting. Freya must choose between sealing the door forever to save the living and opening it to give her people back their names, and in the end she does neither: she becomes the door, binding her gift to the oath Wren rewrites in blood, so the dead pass freely and the Hunt finds nothing left to burn.
about_author: Silas Almeida is a former archivist of maritime records who spent a decade cataloguing the belongings of the drowned, an experience that haunts every page of his fiction. He writes in a coastal town where the fog arrives earlier every year, and he claims the fog dictates his endings.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the guildhouse of Corvane, Freya balances impossible trades — bottled grief, a debt paid in years — while the bone charm at her throat murmurs the dead's names. She hides her gift behind meticulous bookkeeping. Beat: quiet competence masking fear, and the first hint that ledgers can become lists.

chapters.title: What the Crown Announced at Dawn
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Heralds proclaim the Hunt: all with the gift are to be registered, then burned. The guildmaster burns a page and tells Freya to forget it. She cannot. Beat: the safe world cracks; denial curdling into dread.

chapters.title: An Oath Arrives in Winter Clothes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Oath-keeper Wren Halvard arrives to audit the guild, sworn to the crown, hollowed by a vow that punishes disobedience with pain. They sense the gift in the guildhouse like smoke. Beat: duty as a cage; Wren's cold exterior over a starving conscience.

chapters.title: The Bone That Spoke My Mother's Name
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya's carved bone slips and speaks aloud her mother's voice before Wren. The guildmaster sells her out within the hour. Beat: exposure, betrayal, and the strange relief of no longer hiding.

chapters.title: Arrested by the Person Who Should Have Run
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren arrests Freya, but the oath twists when they lie to her about mercy — the vow itself recoils. On the road to the pyre-city, Wren sees the Hunt's first burning from a ridge. Beat: the machinery of duty shown in full horror.

chapters.title: Fire Makes Bad Witnesses
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the holding wagons, Freya hears the dead of the burned — dozens of new voices, all screaming the same name: Vhalen. She tells Wren the pyres are feeding something. Beat: horror reframed as evidence; reluctant alliance begins.

chapters.title: The First Broken Vow
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren frees Freya's wagon in the night, and the oath flays them from the inside — a visible brand spreading up the arm. They run together because neither can survive alone. Beat: the cost of conscience made flesh.

chapters.title: A Guild of Impossible Trades, Liquidated
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They return to find the guildhouse gutted, the guildmaster's ledger seized — and Freya's name on every page, in her own hand, as proof. Beat: grief and rage; her own bookkeeping turned into a noose.

chapters.title: The Map With a Hole in It
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the guildmaster's hidden cache they find a map of the realm with Vhalen cut out — a country erased, its borders stitched shut with oath-magic. The dead's voices point through the hole. Beat: the quest takes shape; hope with a terrible price tag.

chapters.title: Hounds That Smell Promises
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The Hunt's oath-hounds track Wren by their broken vow, not by scent. A river crossing, a near-capture, and Freya learning Wren's brand can be quieted by her touch. Beat: intimacy born of necessity; first tenderness.

chapters.title: The Village That Burned Itself
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A village of the gifted has burned its own names off every record to survive — and asks Wren to swear an oath of silence, which the brand punishes. Wren refuses and is hated for honesty. Beat: the theme of duty sharpened; no clean choices.

chapters.title: Ledger-Keeping for the Fugitive Dead
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya begins a new ledger: every name the Hunt erases, carved into bone so it cannot be unmade. The dead grow calmer, organized. Beat: purpose found — her gift reframed as witness, not curse.

chapters.title: The Huntmaster's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Huntmaster Seraphine Voss offers Wren pardon in exchange for Freya — and reveals the Hunt's true purpose: the pyres are powering a seal on Vhalen's door. Beat: temptation with a face; the plot's engine exposed.

chapters.title: Snow That Falls Upward
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Near the old border, winter behaves wrongly — snow drifting up, rivers running backward — where the erased country presses against the world. The dead's voices are louder here, and kinder. Beat: wonder amid danger; the door is close.

chapters.title: What Wren Swore and to Whom
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confesses the origin of their oath: sworn as a child to the crown after Vhalen fell, when they were a refugee of the drowned country who was allowed to forget. Beat: devastating reveal — Wren is Vhalen-born; the Hunt is hunting their own kin.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The seasonal winter becomes something deliberate — a siege of cold sent to seal the door permanently. Villages freeze mid-task. The dead beg them to hurry. Beat: the clock starts; dread becomes cosmic.

chapters.title: A Trade in Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. To pass the border-stitch, they must trade something impossible to the stitch itself. Freya offers her hearing of the dead; Wren offers the remainder of their oath. The stitch takes a third thing neither offered. Beat: bargain horror; the cost is hidden.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They cross into Vhalen: a drowned land walking, its cities intact under a green-black sky, its people neither living nor dead, waiting for their names to be carried home. Beat: awe and heartbreak; the blurb's promise fulfilled.

chapters.title: Names in the Bone Box
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The waiting dead of Vhalen recognize Wren. Freya reads the ledger aloud, and each name returns a person to themselves — but each reading drains warmth from her body. Beat: love and sacrifice entwined; the mechanism of the ending established.

chapters.title: Seraphine at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Huntmaster Voss follows them through, revealing she is Vhalen-born too — and that she built the seal to keep the dead country dead, believing resurrection is the crown's corruption made literal. Beat: antagonist humanized; ideology versus mercy.

chapters.title: The Middle of the Hunt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Hunt pours through the door after Voss. Wren, oathless now, chooses to stand between — and discovers the broken brand lets them hear the dead too, and command them. Beat: power offered; corruption's first taste.

chapters.title: A General Made of Winter
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The long winter has a will: the crown's first oath-keeper, entombed in the seal, driving the cold. It speaks to Freya in her mother's stolen voice. Beat: the true villain named; personal grief weaponized.

chapters.title: What Power Costs by the Hour
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Commanding the dead, Wren grows colder, more certain, more cruel — ordering dead soldiers like ledger entries. Freya confronts them; they nearly come to blows. Beat: the corruption theme made intimate; the relationship fractures.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The guildmaster, captured and dying, confesses he sold Freya to save the ledger — the ledger of names, which he believed mattered more than any one person. He asks her to keep it. Beat: forgiveness as a hard act; the ledger's meaning deepened.

chapters.title: Vhalen Remembers Its Own Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. As Freya reads more names, Vhalen stabilizes — streets un-drown, the green sky lightens. But each restored name weakens the seal, and the winter general strengthens. Beat: hope and doom rising together; stakes clarified.

chapters.title: The Choice the Dead Offered
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The dead of Vhalen offer Freya a bargain: take all their names into herself, become the door, and no seal or winter can close it — but she will never again be only herself. Beat: the central sacrifice crystallized; she does not answer yet.

chapters.title: Seraphine's Reason
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Voss shows Wren what Vhalen was before it fell: an empire that fed its neighbors' dead to its own door. Her seal is atonement. Wren cannot refute her — only disagree. Beat: moral complexity at full depth; no villain, only wounds.

chapters.title: Pyres in the Green Country
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The Hunt begins burning Vhalen's waiting dead, and each pyre feeds the winter general. Freya's ledger becomes triage — which names can she save first? Beat: despair, triage, the weight of witness; her lowest point.

chapters.title: The Brand That Chose
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren's broken brand turns fully against the crown's oath, burning away everything the vow demanded — leaving Wren free, and empty, unsure what remains when duty is gone. Beat: identity stripped; love becomes the only compass left.

chapters.title: A Confession in a Frozen Orchard
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In a dead orchard, Freya and Wren finally say plainly what they are to each other — knowing one of them may not survive the week. Beat: the love declared without promise of time; quiet before the storm.

chapters.title: The General Offers a Trade
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The winter general offers Freya her mother's true voice — alive, restored — if she surrenders the ledger and lets the seal close forever. Freya hesitates one terrible moment. Beat: temptation at its most personal; Wren watches her waver.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Is For
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya refuses: names are not hers to hoard or trade; they belong to the people who bore them. She begins reading the ledger aloud in the general's face, name after name, as the cold closes in. Beat: defiance as devotion; the climax's fuse lit.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Stitched Border
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren leads Vhalen's dead against the Hunt at the border-stitch, fighting beside the people they were sworn to burn, the brand blazing like a banner. Beat: duty rewritten; the oath inverted into protection.

chapters.title: Seraphine Breaks Her Own Seal
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Watching the Hunt burn children's names, Voss shatters her own seal from the inside, dying to undo her life's work, and entrusts Wren with the seal's keystone. Beat: the antagonist's redemption; the way to the door opened.

chapters.title: The Keystone and the Knife
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The keystone can close the door forever — safety for the living, erasure for the dead — or be given to Freya to become the door. Wren must choose for her, because she is too deep in the reading to choose for herself. Beat: love against duty at its sharpest.

chapters.title: The Long Winter's Last Assault
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The general spends everything in one final freeze; the orchard, the city, the ledger itself icing over. Wren reaches Freya through the storm carrying the keystone. Beat: climax begins; everything narrows to two people and a choice.

chapters.title: Neither Open nor Shut
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren refuses both options and does the impossible thing: swears a new oath on the keystone — to hold the door with Freya, neither open nor shut, the dead passing freely and the living free to leave. The keystone accepts. Beat: the third answer; the theme resolved in action.

chapters.title: The Door With Two Names On It
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya and Wren become the door's living hinges, sharing the burden — she hears the dead, Wren answers them, and the winter general dissolves into ordinary, honest snow. Beat: climax resolved through shared power, not sacrifice alone.

chapters.title: After the Hunt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Spring comes wrong and then right. The Hunt is disbanded in disgrace; the guild of impossible trades reopens with a new ledger — one that records names given back, not taken. Beat: the world exhales; grief given shape and ceremony.

chapters.title: A Wolf for the Oath
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the door, Freya and Wren take up permanent residence between countries, keeping the ledger together; the last entry is her mother's name, read at last into peace. Beat: belonging found not in a place but in a shared vow — the title's meaning fulfilled.
